Letter from Joseph Smith to Emma Smith, Apr. 4, 1839, Liberty Jail, Liberty, Missouri; Beinecke Library, Yale University, New Haven, Connecticut; copy in Church Archives, The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, Salt Lake City, Utah. In this letter, when the Prophet referred to being imprisoned for over five months, he was counting the time he was imprisoned in Independence and Richmond, Missouri, as well as in Liberty.

Sidney Rigdon was incarcerated in Liberty Jail with the other brethren on December 1, 1838. However, on January 25, 1839, about two months before the Prophet wrote this letter, Sidney was given permission to leave the jail on bail because he was severely ill. Because continued threats made him afraid to leave the security of the jail, Sidney chose to remain in jail until February 5.
